column1: #   One value, one name, across the resolved MIOS_* environment that
#   usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot produces from the SSOT.  The tree
#   violates that property 816 times today, so the gate RATCHETS rather than
#   blocking: every duplicate-value group that exists now is recorded below
#   with its exact key set, and the group count is pinned by the ceiling.
#   VIOLATION if a duplicate group appears whose value is not recorded here;
#   VIOLATION if a new key joins a group that is recorded here;
#   VIOLATION if the group count differs from the ceiling in either direction;
#   VIOLATION if the resolver, this ledger, or python3 is missing or fails --
#   a gate with no data must never report green, which is exactly how the
#   previous version of this check stayed green over all 816 groups.
#   Do NOT add a row to silence a new duplicate.  Collapse the duplicate.  If
#   the two keys really are distinct facts that happen to share a value, say so
#   and regenerate -- the added row then shows up in the diff for review.
#   #!ceiling is the number of groups and it is EXACT.  More groups is a
#   regression.  FEWER groups is also a failure, because a ceiling that never
#   comes down is how 816 accumulated: fixing duplicates must be paid for by
#   tightening this number in the same commit.
#   The ceiling lives here rather than in mios.toml because a number in the
#   SSOT that counts the resolved duplicate VALUES in the resolved environment is
#   self-referential -- "816" already occurs four times as an env value, so
#   declaring the ceiling in mios.toml would perturb the very set it counts.
# REGENERATE (after a legitimate SSOT change, and review the diff)
#   value<TAB>key_count<TAB>comma-separated MIOS_* keys, ordered by descending
#   key count then value.  The value field escapes backslash as \, TAB as \t
#   and CR as \r.  Values the gate does not treat as duplicates at all --
#   the empty string, true/false, 0/1 and the well-known ports 22/53/80/443/
